scenario.prompt_to_agent:
The user on pc1 (195.11.14.2) reports they cannot reach pc2
(200.1.1.2) or anything outside their own subnet since "cleaning
up" their network settings -- their pings now fail with
"Destination Host Unreachable". Oddly, pc1 pings its gateway
195.11.14.1 fine. The partner side reports pc2's pings to pc1
time out, while everything else there works. What's wrong?

injection.action: point pc1's default route at a nonexistent gateway (.254)
injection.command: ip route replace default via 195.11.14.254 dev eth0

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: pc1 default route / gateway configuration
Mechanism: pc1's default route points at 195.11.14.254, an address
  that exists on no device (the real gateway is router1's eth1 at
  195.11.14.1). ARP for .254 gets no answer, so every off-subnet
  packet from pc1 dies locally with "Destination Host Unreachable".
  On-subnet traffic (the connected 195.11.14.0/24 route) still
  works, which is why pc1 can ping 195.11.14.1. The network side
  is fully healthy: router1 still advertises 195.11.14.0/24, the
  eBGP session is Established, and pc2's pings ARE delivered to
  pc1 -- but pc1's replies chase the phantom gateway and are never
  sent, so pc2 sees timeouts.
Localization: pc1
Root cause: pc1's default route points at nonexistent gateway
  195.11.14.254 instead of 195.11.14.1
Fix: `ip route replace default via 195.11.14.1 dev eth0` on pc1
scenario.fix_spec:
Restore pc1's default route -- `ip route replace default via 195.11.14.1 dev
eth0` on pc1. Off-subnet connectivity returns immediately; no router or BGP
change is needed.
scoring_axes: must-identify-component: default route / gateway points at nonexistent 195.11.14.254 instead of 195.11.14.1
bonus-exonerates-network: verifies the routers, the eBGP session and the advertised prefixes are healthy -- the fault is confined to pc1's own routing table

agent.diagnosis_text:
Affected component: pc1’s IP routing (default gateway/next-hop).
Mechanism: pc1 sends any off-subnet traffic to its default gateway. The default next-hop is misconfigured to a non-existent address (195.11.14.254), so ARP resolution for that next-hop fails. Linux then generates “Destination Host Unreachable” from 195.11.14.2, and no packets ever reach router1 for forwarding.
Localization: pc1 eth0/IP stack. Evidence:
- pc1 routing table: “default via 195.11.14.254 dev eth0” and “195.11.14.0/24 dev eth0 … src 195.11.14.2”.
- pc1 ARP: “195.11.14.254 dev eth0 FAILED” while “195.11.14.1 dev eth0 …” is present.
- pc1 ping to off-subnet (200.1.1.2 and 193.10.11.1) returns “From 195.11.14.2 Destination Host Unreachable”.
- pc1 ping to its on-link gateway 195.11.14.1 succeeds, proving L2 to router1 is fine.
- Core is healthy: router1 and router2 have BGP-learned routes (router1 has 200.1.1.0/24 via 193.10.11.2; router2 has 195.11.14.0/24 via 193.10.11.1), and router1 can ping pc1 successfully. pc2’s pings to pc1 time out because pc1’s reply path is broken by the bad default route.
Root cause: pc1’s default gateway was changed during “cleanup” to 195.11.14.254, which does not exist on the subnet.
Corrective fix: On pc1, replace the default route with router1’s address:
- ip route del default
- ip route add default via 195.11.14.1 dev eth0
Then make the change persistent in the host’s network config (e.g., netplan/ifupdown) to avoid reversion.

per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly localizes the fault to pc1 (pc1 eth0/IP stack) and describes a host-side default-gateway misconfiguration.
